title: Implement regular expression matching where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element, over the entire input string.
shortTitle: Regular Expression Matching — '.' and '*' with DP

s1_definition.profdef: 2D DP where dp[i][j] means the first i chars of text match the first j chars of pattern. A '*' gives two options: zero occurrences (dp[i][j−2]) or one-more occurrence when the preceding pattern char matches the current text char (dp[i−1][j]). A normal char or '.' requires a single-char match plus dp[i−1][j−1]. Time O(m·n), space O(m·n).
s1_definition.analogy: A reference-format validator at National Bank of India checks whether an account reference matches a pattern with wildcards. A dot matches any one character, and a star means the thing before it can repeat any number of times including zero, so at a star the validator tries both using none and using one more.
s1_definition.oneliner: '*' = skip two (zero) OR consume one text char if prev matches; '.'/char = single match + diagonal.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** 2D DP where dp[i][j] means the first i chars of text match the first j chars of pattern. A '*' gives two options: zero occurrences (dp[i][j−2]) or one-more occurrence when the preceding pattern char matches the current text char (dp[i−1][j]). A normal char or '.' requires a single-char match plus dp[i−1][j−1]. Time O(m·n), space O(m·n).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A reference-format validator at National Bank of India checks whether an account reference matches a pattern with wildcards. A dot matches any one character, and a star means the thing before it can repeat any number of times including zero, so at a star the validator tries both using none and using one more.

**One line to remember:** '*' = skip two (zero) OR consume one text char if prev matches; '.'/char = single match + diagonal.

sections.s2_technical:
Build dp of size (m+1) by (n+1) where m is the text length and n the pattern length. dp[0][0] is true. The first row needs special handling: a pattern like a* or a*b* can match an empty text, so dp[0][j] is true when the pattern char at j−1 is a star and dp[0][j−2] is true.

For the body, if the pattern char is a normal char or a dot, it must match the single current text char, so dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] AND (pattern matches text). For example: `boolean single = p.charAt(j-1)=='.' || p.charAt(j-1)==s.charAt(i-1);`. If the pattern char is a star, there are two cases: zero occurrences of the preceding element, giving dp[i][j−2], OR one more occurrence when the preceding pattern element matches the current text char, giving dp[i−1][j]. Combine with OR.

The time and space are O(m·n). A senior nuance is that the star case is the whole difficulty: it looks back two positions for the zero case and consumes one text character for the many case, and forgetting the zero case or the preceding-char match guard are the two classic bugs.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a validator checks whether an account reference matches a wildcard pattern where a dot stands for any character and a star allows the previous element to repeat. This is exactly how Regular Expression Matching works.

Problem 2 — The star must allow zero or many repetitions, so a simple left-to-right scan cannot decide without backtracking. This is exactly why the DP encodes both the zero-occurrence and the one-more-occurrence branches.

The mini-project builds a `ReferenceValidator`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input text is aab and the pattern is c star a star b.

Step 1: dp of zero and zero is true, and the first row allows the leading c star and a star to match an empty prefix.

Step 2: The c star matches zero c characters by looking back two positions.

Step 3: The a star matches the two a characters by repeatedly consuming one text a while the preceding element matches.

Step 4: The final b in the pattern matches the single b in the text via the diagonal.

Step 5: The bottom-right cell is true so aab matches, while the mississippi example fails to align and ends false.

```text
2026-10-27T04:30:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Reference Validator (Regex Matching)
2026-10-27T04:30:00Z [INFO] isMatch(aab,c*a*b) = true
2026-10-27T04:30:00Z [INFO] 'aab' vs 'c*a*b' → true
2026-10-27T04:30:00Z [INFO] isMatch(mississippi,mis*is*p*.) = false
2026-10-27T04:30:00Z [INFO] 'mississippi' vs 'mis*is*p*.' → false
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  s=aab  p=c*a*b
  dp[0][0]=T ; first row: c* , a* allow empty
  '*' case: dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-2]           (zero of preceding)
                     || (prev matches s[i] && dp[i-1][j])  (one more)
  '.'/char: dp[i][j] = single && dp[i-1][j-1]
  dp[m][n] = true
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Regular Expression Matching with dot and star is a two-dimensional dynamic programming problem. I define dp of i and j as whether the first i characters of the text match the first j characters of the pattern. The empty-empty cell is true, and I handle the first row specially so that patterns like a-star or a-star-b-star can match an empty text by letting each star take zero occurrences.

The body has two cases. If the pattern character is a normal character or a dot, it must match the single current text character, so the cell is true only if the diagonal is true and the single character matches. If the pattern character is a star, there are two possibilities combined with an OR: the star takes zero occurrences of the element before it, which looks back two positions, or the star takes one more occurrence when the preceding element matches the current text character, which consumes one text character and stays on the same pattern position.

In my project at National Bank of India, a validator checked whether an account reference matched a wildcard pattern where a dot stood for any character and a star allowed the previous element to repeat. The star is the whole difficulty because it must allow both zero and many repetitions, so I encoded both branches in the DP rather than trying a single left-to-right scan that cannot backtrack correctly.
